text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-INC-8912 — redis-prod cluster (maxclients) firing. Severity: P1. Notifying eng-oncall rotation and SRE channel. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-INC-8912

pagerduty: PagerDuty: alert PD-INC-8912 created and routed to eng-oncall.

maya: ack — I’m on it. Tailing redis logs now.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: acknowledged by maya.

jae: seeing a big spike in CLIENTS on shard-3. grabbing `redis-cli -h shard-3 INFO clients` now.

jae: ```
# redis-cli -h shard-3 INFO clients
connected_clients:10192
client_longest_output_list:0
client_biggest_input_buf:0
blocked_clients:0
maxclients:10000
```

omar: ugh, connected_clients above maxclients — connections are being refused. app logs show a ton of ECONNREFUSED. Looks like a sudden fanout job from analytics service.

lina: can we throttle at the gateway? add a quick rule to reduce concurrent requests to the realtime path (/v1/stream) to 50c per instance. That should buy us time.

maya: customer impact: realtime webhooks and streaming to customers are seeing ~8-12% 5xx. (Grafana: 2026-03-15T10:12–10:18 window). Some large customers reporting delayed updates.

omar: rolling temporary mitigation: `redis-cli -h shard-3 CONFIG SET maxclients 12000` on primaries to reduce immediate rejects. Pushing now to shard-1..4. Note: this is temporary — kernel fd limits need to be bumped for persistence.

omar: command I ran: ```
for host in shard-1 shard-2 shard-3 shard-4; do 
  redis-cli -h $host CONFIG SET maxclients 12000 || echo fail $host;
done
```

jae: ran `redis-cli INFO clients` again — connected_clients dropped a bit after some client retries but still high: 9700/12000. No immediate evictions, memory within normal.

oncall-runbook-bot: Runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/redis-maxclients — steps: throttle -> CONFIG SET -> monitor -> escalate to SRE lead if persists > 10m.

susan: escalated by PD due to ongoing errors. Taking over incident. Suspending noisy non-critical analytics job rn. @omar please confirm you can throttle or pause the analytics fanout.

omar: pausing analytics fanout job now (triggered via deploy/analytics/fanout PAUSE). Also enabling client-side jitter on retry config for the next 1 hour.

lina: gateway rule deployed: `limit: path:/v1/stream concurrent:50` on edge nodes. Rolling restart completed, should reduce new connection pressure.

maya: noted we've reduced new connection attempts, but tail shows some long-lived clients not closing properly. Might need to add a periodic connection pruning script or adjust keepalive.

jae: quick check of kernel limits on nodes — running `sysctl fs.file-max` and `ulimit -n`; if we want persistent higher maxclients we need to update `/etc/security/limits.conf` and systemd overrides.

jae: ```
# on redis host
$ ulimit -n
65536
$ sysctl fs.file-max
fs.file-max = 2097152
```

omar: applied `CONFIG SET maxclients 12000` to all primaries. Confirmed no more immediate rejects. Will open follow-up change to bump OS limits and set config in redis.conf for persistence.

susan: handoff summary for execs: short story — analytics fanout caused connection storm to redis causing maxclients saturation on primaries; temporary mitigations: CONFIG SET to raise maxclients, paused analytics job, deployed gateway throttling. Customer impact: ~10% errors on realtime streaming for ~15 minutes. No data lost. Next steps: schedule persistent kernel + redis.conf change, add connection pooling, and rate-limit heavy producers. I’ll own the follow-up.

maya: creating incident ticket RD-INC-2026-55 and attaching logs + grafana panels. Link: https://issues.redwood/RD-INC-2026-55

oncall-runbook-bot: Recommended post-incident checklist created and assigned to susan.

susan: marking PD incident as acknowledged and silencing duplicate pages for 30m to reduce noise. Monitoring now; will update within 30m with RCA plan. :white_check_mark:

maya: handing over to susan — I’m back on rotation tasks, but will help with postmortem.

susan: thanks — if anyone sees client reconnect storms again ping me directly. Closing this thread once we have follow-ups in Jira. :thumbsup:
